newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Chirac pledges support for fast Romania NATO entry.
newsitem.headline: Chirac pledges support for fast Romania NATO entry.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac said on Friday he would press for Romania to be among the first ex-communist countries to be admitted to an expanded NATO and pledged to defend its interests within the Alliance.
"I want Romania to join us within NATO from 1999. I am saying this here in Bucharest as I said it London, Washington and Bonn," Chirac told Romania's parliament at the start of a two-day visit.

Chirac said Romania deserved to be included in NATO's first expansion due to be announced in July after resolving disputes with Hungary in a treaty last year and bringing ethnic Hungarians into its new coalition government.

"France will extend you all its support and champion your interests within the European Union and NATO to help you overcome difficulties," he told parliament's two chambers, dominated by centrists since last November's election.

The United States considers Romania a long shot for early membership behind favourites Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic although it has appeared to improve its prospects after the centrists threw ex-communists out of office.

Chirac said the Alliance's expansion had to take account of the interests of "the great Russian nation", an allusion to Moscow's opposition to enlargment. Unlike in pledges made during recent visits to Poland and Hungary, Chirac gave no target date for less-developed Romania to join the EU.
